source.place: Tag 06Y6 and Tag 0DJ8, transport through derived tensor cohomology

proof.text: For an additive module functor F that preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes, use the existing source-library F.leftDerivedFunctor and its counit. The chosen resolution P of M is K-flat and its augmentation s:P→M is a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality at a times identity gives resolution(a times identity) followed by s equal to s followed by a times identity. A-linearity of s identifies the latter with a times identity of P followed by s. Invert Q(s) to conclude equality of the two maps on P in the derived category. Apply F.leftDerivedFunctor and use naturality and invertibility of its counit on P to conclude equality of the derived images of the termwise F maps. The two natural homology factorization isomorphisms transport this to equality on ordinary homology. If F sends a times identity to b times identity on modules, componentwise extensionality and ShortComplex.homologyMap_smul give b times identity on this homology. This is the proved private helper resolution_homology_scalar, with the standard derived localizations and exact countable colimits on ModuleCat.

For the source take F=extendScalars(R→B). Supply PreservesKFlatQuasiIso using the already proved scalarExtension_quasiIso_of_kFlat helper from KFlatScalarExtensionDerivedIso, accessed by a proof-only import all. Restriction maps algebraMap R A r times identity to r times identity by the definition of the restricted action. On tensor generators, balancing gives F(r times identity)=algebraMap R B r times identity. Apply the preceding helper to the restricted complex.

For the target take F=restrictScalars(R→A) followed by extendScalars(R→B), now viewed as a module functor from A to B. To show that it preserves quasi-isomorphisms between A-K-flat complexes, apply scalarExtension_quasiIso_of_kFlat over A with coefficients A tensor_R B, then restrict to B. The pure-tensor formulas of exists_baseTensorOrdinaryIso give an isomorphism of arrows from this map to extension after restriction, proving the required quasi-isomorphism property. At the module level restriction and tensor balancing again send algebraMap R A r times identity to algebraMap R B r times identity. Apply resolution_homology_scalar to the A-resolution and combine the source and target equalities as a conjunction. No natural choice of the ordinary tensor isomorphisms is required: only their generator formulas are used to prove the arrow square. Zero rings, zero complexes, r=0 and r=1 require no exception.

title: Scalar compatibility of affine tensor cohomology
statement: For commutative R-algebras A and B and every integer i, each functor K among source and target of [def-pc-ring-tensor-cohomology] sends multiplication by algebraMap R A r on every A-complex M to multiplication by algebraMap R B r on K(M), for every r in R. No additivity hypothesis, flatness or boundedness is imposed.

lean.statement: theorem affineTensorCohomology_scalar_parts (R A B : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] (i : ℤ) : (∀ (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (r : R), (source R A B i).map (algebraMap R A r • 𝟙 M) = algebraMap R B r • 𝟙 ((source R A B i).obj M)) ∧ (∀ (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (r : R), (target R A B i).map (algebraMap R A r • 𝟙 M) = algebraMap R B r • 𝟙 ((target R A B i).obj M))
